breakfast.name: Pão de Queijo (Cheese Bread)
instructions: Heat milk with oil and salt until just boiling
Pour over tapioca starch, stir vigorously — it will form a sticky mass
Cool enough to handle, then knead in eggs one at a time
Fold in cheese
Roll into small balls — they should be slightly sticky
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 min until puffed, golden, and cracked on top
Eat immediately — they deflate as they cool
breakfast.description: Chewy, cheesy, gluten-free rolls from Minas Gerais — the tapioca starch makes them uniquely puffy and stretchy inside. Found at every bakery and gas station in Brazil.

breakfast.name: Café da Manhã (Brazilian Breakfast Spread)
ingredients: Cake (bolo de cenoura or bolo de fubá)
instructions: Slice and toast pão francês
Butter and fill with ham and cheese
Slice papaya
Cut a generous slice of cake — yes, cake for breakfast
Make café com leite: equal parts strong filtered coffee and hot milk
Arrange everything on the table — breakfast is leisurely
breakfast.description: Brazilian breakfast is a spread: crusty rolls, strong milky coffee, fresh papaya, ham, cheese, and always a slice of cake. It's simpler than it sounds and more satisfying than it should be.

breakfast.name: Tapioca Crepe (Beiju)
ingredients: 1 cup hydrated tapioca starch (goma de tapioca)
Filling: queijo coalho, coconut, condensed milk, or butter and cheese
instructions: Heat non-stick pan — no oil needed
Sprinkle tapioca starch evenly in a thin layer through a sieve
Cook 1-2 min until it forms a solid white disk
Add filling to one half, fold over
Cook 1 more min until cheese melts
Serve immediately
breakfast.description: Northeastern Brazilian crêpe made from tapioca starch — naturally gluten-free, chewy, and filled with anything from cheese to condensed milk. It becomes transparent as it cooks.

lunch.name: Feijoada Completa
ingredients: Assorted pork: ribs, sausage (linguiça), carne seca (jerky), pig ear, pig tail, bacon
Accompaniments: white rice, farofa, couve (collard greens), orange slices, vinagrete (tomato-onion salsa)
instructions: Cook soaked beans with bay leaves until almost tender, 1.5 hours
In separate pots, cook the tougher cuts (ears, tails) until soft
Sauté onion and garlic in lard, add to beans
Add all meats to the bean pot gradually — sausage and bacon last
Add halved orange — it cuts the richness
Simmer everything together 30+ min until thick and rich
Make accompaniments: sauté shredded collard greens in garlic; toast farofa (cassava flour) in butter; dice tomato-onion vinagrete
Serve beans and meats in the center, surrounded by bowls of rice, collard greens, farofa, orange slices, and vinagrete
This is a Saturday ritual — never rushed
lunch.description: Brazil's national dish — a magnificent slow-cooked black bean stew with every cut of pork imaginable. Always Saturday lunch, always communal.

lunch.name: Moqueca Baiana (Bahian Fish Stew)
instructions: Marinate fish in lime and salt 15 min
In a clay pot (panela de barro), layer: onion, tomato, pepper, fish
Pour coconut milk and dendê oil over — do NOT stir
Cover and cook 25-30 min on medium — the layers meld without stirring
The dendê oil floats to the top, creating a vibrant orange layer
Scatter with cilantro and malagueta pepper
Bring the clay pot to the table
Serve with white rice and pirão (fish gravy thickened with cassava flour)
lunch.description: Bahian fish stew cooked in a clay pot — African-influenced, vivid orange from dendê oil, never stirred so the layers stay beautiful. The clay pot matters.

lunch.name: Churrasco (Brazilian BBQ)
ingredients: Vinagrete (diced tomato, onion, pepper, vinegar, oil)
instructions: Cut picanha into thick C-shaped pieces, following the fat cap curve
Season with coarse salt only — nothing else touches picanha
Skewer in the C-shape, fat side out
Grill over charcoal, rotating the skewer slowly
Carve thin slices off the outside as each layer cooks — this is the rodízio method
Season and grill flank steak, sausage, and chicken hearts on separate skewers
Serve sliced at the table with farofa and vinagrete
lunch.description: Brazilian churrasco is about fire, salt, and good meat — especially picanha, the prized fat-capped cut that defined Brazilian BBQ worldwide.

dinner.name: Acarajé (Fried Bean Cakes)
ingredients: Filling: vatapá (shrimp-peanut-coconut cream), caruru (okra stew), dried shrimp, vinagrete, hot pepper
instructions: Blend peeled black-eyed peas with onion and salt to a thick paste
Beat vigorously — the airy texture is crucial, it should be lighter than hummus
Heat dendê oil to 180°C in a deep pan
Drop rounded spoonfuls into the oil
Fry until deep golden and crispy, 5-6 min
Split open like a sandwich
Fill with vatapá, caruru, dried shrimp, vinagrete, and pepper sauce
dinner.description: Afro-Brazilian bean fritters fried in palm oil and stuffed with shrimp — sold by baianas (women in white traditional dress) on the streets of Salvador. UNESCO-recognized cultural heritage.

dinner.name: Frango à Passarinho (Crispy Chicken Bites)
ingredients: 1kg chicken (cut into very small bone-in pieces)
instructions: Cut chicken into small pieces — bone-in bites, not boneless
Marinate in garlic, lime, and salt for 1+ hour
Fry in hot oil until deeply golden and crispy
Toss with extra fried garlic chips
Serve with lime wedges
dinner.description: Bar-style crispy chicken bites — named 'little bird' for the small bone-in pieces. Found at every boteco (neighborhood bar) in Brazil.

dinner.name: Vatapá (Shrimp Coconut Cream)
instructions: Soak dried shrimp, grind half, leave half whole
Blend soaked bread with coconut milk until smooth
Sauté onion, garlic, ginger in dendê oil
Add ground peanuts and cashews
Add coconut-bread mixture, cook until thick
Add shrimp, season with pepper
Simmer until creamy and golden
Serve with white rice or as filling for acarajé
dinner.description: Rich Bahian shrimp cream thickened with bread, peanuts, and cashews — West African roots in Brazilian cuisine.

snacks.name: Coxinha (Chicken Croquette)
ingredients: Filling: shredded chicken, cream cheese, onion, parsley
instructions: Heat broth and butter to boiling, add flour all at once
Stir vigorously until dough pulls from the pan in a smooth ball
Cool dough until handleable
Flatten a piece in your palm, add chicken filling
Wrap dough around filling, shape into a teardrop — this shape is essential, it represents a chicken drumstick
Dip in egg wash, roll in fine breadcrumbs
Deep fry at 180°C until deep golden
The outside should shatter, the inside should be creamy
snacks.description: Teardrop-shaped chicken croquettes — Brazil's most popular snack food. The shape mimics a chicken drumstick, and the dough-to-filling ratio is fiercely debated.

snacks.name: Pastel (Fried Pastry)
ingredients: Wrapper: flour, cachaça, oil, salt, warm water (or store-bought)
Fillings: ground beef with olives, hearts of palm with cheese, or shrimp
instructions: Mix dough (the cachaça makes it extra crispy), rest 30 min
Roll very thin, cut rectangles
Fill one side, fold, seal edges with fork
Deep fry until blistered and golden — the wrapper should puff up
Serve immediately with hot sauce
snacks.description: Paper-thin crispy fried pastry with endless filling options — the Saturday morning feira (market) tradition. Best eaten standing up at the market stall.

snacks.name: Pão de Queijo Recheado (Stuffed Cheese Bread)
ingredients: Pão de queijo dough: tapioca starch, milk, oil, eggs, queijo minas or Parmesan
Filling: requeijão (Brazilian cream cheese), guava paste, or Catupiry cheese
instructions: Make pão de queijo dough: heat milk and oil, pour over tapioca starch, mix, add eggs and cheese
Shape into balls, press a hole, fill with requeijão or guava paste
Close dough around filling
Bake at 180°C for 20 min until puffed and golden
When you bite in, the filling oozes out — the requeijão version is the viral one
snacks.description: Stuffed pão de queijo — the TikTok-viral version with molten cream cheese or guava paste inside the already-chewy cheese bread. The cheese pull videos broke the internet.

snacks.name: Picanha na Brasa (Viral Steak Cut)
ingredients: 1kg picanha (top sirloin cap, fat cap on)
instructions: Do NOT trim the fat cap — this is essential
Cut into thick steaks with the grain, keeping the C-shaped curve and fat
Season only with coarse salt — nothing else
Fold each steak into a C-shape on a skewer, fat side out
Grill over high heat, fat side first, until the fat renders and chars
Flip, cook to medium-rare inside
Slice thin against the grain at the table
The fat bastes the meat as it cooks — this is why picanha is the world's most viral steak cut
snacks.description: The cut that made Brazilian steakhouses famous worldwide — top sirloin cap with the fat left on. The viral C-fold skewer technique and the fat-basting have made it the most searched steak on YouTube.

desserts.name: Brigadeiro (Chocolate Truffle)
instructions: Combine condensed milk, cocoa, and butter in non-stick pan
Cook on medium heat, stirring constantly
Scrape the bottom — it burns easily
Cook until mixture pulls away from the pan as one mass, 12-15 min
Transfer to buttered plate, cool until handleable
Butter your hands, roll into small balls
Roll in chocolate sprinkles
Place in small paper cups
desserts.description: Brazil's most beloved sweet — invented in the 1940s for a political campaign. Every birthday party, every celebration, every Tuesday when you're sad. The name means 'brigadier.'

desserts.name: Pudim de Leite (Milk Flan)
ingredients: Custard: 1 can condensed milk, 1 can whole milk (use the condensed milk can to measure), 3 eggs
instructions: Melt sugar in flan mold until deep amber caramel, swirl to coat
Blend condensed milk, whole milk, and eggs — that's it, just three ingredients
Pour through strainer into caramelized mold
Cover tightly with foil
Bake in water bath at 160°C for 60 min
Cool, refrigerate overnight
Unmold — the caramel sauce cascades over the custard
desserts.description: Condensed milk flan — denser and sweeter than French crème caramel. The recipe is on every can of Leite Moça condensed milk in Brazil.

desserts.name: Bolo de Rolo (Roll Cake)
ingredients: Batter: 250g butter, 250g sugar, 6 egg yolks, 6 egg whites (whipped), 250g flour
Filling: guava paste (goiabada) melted with a little water into thick paste
instructions: Cream butter and sugar, add yolks
Fold in whipped whites alternately with flour
Spread paper-thin layer of batter on baking sheet
Bake at 200°C for just 3-4 min — barely set
Spread thin layer of guava paste
Roll tightly while still warm
Repeat with another layer, rolling around the first roll
Keep layering and rolling — a proper bolo de rolo has 10+ paper-thin layers
Slice to reveal the dramatic spiral of dozens of thin layers
desserts.description: A cake with dozens of paper-thin layers spiraling around guava paste — Pernambuco's pride. Cross-section photos went viral for the hypnotic spiral pattern. Each layer is individually baked and rolled.

drinks.name: Caipirinha
instructions: Cut lime into 8 wedges, removing white pith from center
Place in rocks glass with sugar
Muddle firmly — press and twist to extract juice and oils, don't pulverize
Add cachaça
Fill with crushed ice
Stir vigorously — the dilution is part of the drink
Serve in the same glass you muddled in
drinks.description: Brazil's national cocktail — cachaça (sugarcane spirit), lime, and sugar. Simple, potent, and dangerously easy to drink. Never made with vodka.

drinks.name: Guaraná Antartica
instructions: Serve ice cold
Brazil's most popular soft drink — outsells Coca-Cola in the country
drinks.description: Made from guaraná berries from the Amazon — sweet, fruity, and uniquely Brazilian. The national soft drink.

drinks.name: Açaí na Tigela (Açaí Bowl)
ingredients: Splash of guaraná syrup or apple juice
Toppings: granola, sliced banana, honey, guaraná powder
instructions: Blend frozen açaí pulp with banana and a splash of liquid — it should be thick, like soft serve
Pour into a bowl
Top with granola, sliced banana, and a drizzle of honey
Eat with a spoon — it's too thick for a straw
drinks.description: Originally a post-surf fuel in Pará state, now a worldwide phenomenon. Real açaí is deep purple and barely sweet — the hyper-sweetened version abroad is a different thing.
